title: Lease-based Surge Credits + Graceful Preemption: Dedicated Capacity PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Implement a lease-based surge credit system and a configurable graceful-preemption window for Dedicated capacity tenants. This feature lets tenants purchase or be allocated short-term surge 'leases' that temporarily raise their effective capacity and provide bounded, auditable fallback behavior when physical capacity is constrained. The offering ties together allocation APIs, runtime admission control, billing/ledgering, and operator-visible telemetry. Motivation: customers asked for predictable competitive bursts without permanent reservation churn and with clear preemption semantics so production apps degrade predictably. This PRD defines requirements, non-goals, UX, telemetry, and rollout checklist.
goals: Provide tenants a lease abstraction to acquire short-term surge capacity with explicit start/end and credit accounting
Ensure preemption uses a graceful window allowing in-flight requests to finish or be retried according to tenant policy
Expose developer-friendly APIs (create/extend/cancel lease) and Console UX for visibility and audit trails
Keep unit cost predictable and produce billing-ready ledger events for surge consumption
non_goals: This PRD does not change core reserved pool long-term contracts (monthly/annual) or billing model for committed capacity
Not addressing global rebalancer changes — regional-only for initial launch
No automatic market-based surge pricing in v1 (price set by admin or preconfigured plans)
user_stories: As a platform engineer I want to grant a temporary 2x compute lease to a customer for a 1-hour window so that their PLG campaign handles peak traffic
As a tenant developer I want in-console visibility and API hooks to see lease usage and remaining credits so I can degrade features proactively
As an SRE I want graceful-preemption windows to avoid widespread tail-latency spikes during eviction events
As a billing analyst I want event-level surge consumption records so invoices are auditable
requirements: Lease entity: start_time, end_time, capacity_multiplier (or fixed slots), owner_tenant_id, lease_id, plan_id, status
Console: Lease creation flow with plan selector, duration slider, estimated cost, and renewal options
Runtime admission: honor active leases by routing requests into tenant's lease allocation until exhausted; when physical capacity unavailable respect preemption policy
Preemption policy: configurable per-tenant flags: grace_window_seconds (default 30s), retry_policy (immediate/requeue/backoff), preserve_inflight (true/false)
Ledger events: emit structured events for lease allocation, start, consumption (per-minute or per-request granularity), extension, cancellation, and expiration
Telemetry: per-lease consumption timeseries, preemption incidents, failed allocations, and end-to-end latency percentiles
Safety: leases cannot allow overall system overcommit to exceed operator-configured headroom; cluster-level guardrails enforced
Audit & RBAC: only tenants with 'surge:lease' entitlement can create paid leases; admin roles can override
edge_cases: Lease created but cluster lacks capacity at start_time: implement queued soft-start with notification and optional auto-refund
Concurrent extend requests: implement optimistic concurrency with version tokens and clear error semantics
Lease cancellation mid-flight: respect preserve_inflight flag to allow outstanding requests to finish within grace_window_seconds
Cross-tenant isolation: ensure KV-caching and shared batching honor tenant fences even under lease-induced co-location
Partial fulfillment: when only part of requested surge capacity can be allocated, expose partial-lease status and prorated ledger events
acceptance_criteria: API surface implemented and passes contract tests: create/extend/cancel/list leases with valid auth and RBAC checks
Runtime honors active leases in a cluster with simulated constrained capacity: requests bound to lease allocation receive expected throughput while respecting system headroom
Graceful preemption works: in forced-eviction test, in-flight requests complete within grace_window_seconds or receive documented retry responses
Billing ledger emits events that reconcile with observed consumption within 1% margin in an e2e synthetic load test
Console shows lease lifecycle and real-time consumption graphs within 5s of event emission
Failover behavior validated: if primary region cannot honor a lease, fallback routing follows tenant policy (fallback_model or deny) and incidents are logged
success_metrics: Percentage of lease starts that are fully honored at start_time >= 98% in pilot clusters
Average preemption-induced user-visible error rate < 0.5% after rollout
Billing reconciliation delta < 1% vs synthetic ground-truth
Tenants adopting leases for burst use cases >= 10% of new Dedicated customers in first quarter after launch
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flag gated API + internal-only console for engineering customers; run smoke tests in canary cluster
Phase 1: invite 5 pilot tenants (sales/solutions-chosen) with different profiles (short spikes, long sustained spikes) for two-week pilots
Phase 2: open beta to all Dedicated tenants in region-us-west-2 behind opt-in
Phase 3: GA with billing enabled and operator guardrails; cross-region support added after GA
Rollback criteria: high preemption incidents (>2% of requests) or billing reconciliation delta >2% trigger temporary disable and incident review
dependencies: ENG-4558 (console UI: plan selector and charts)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: simpler fixed-slot lease vs multiplier model. We pick multiplier (e.g., 1.5x) for v1 to reduce fragmentation while leaving slots for advanced plans.
Operator guardrails: cluster headroom default 10% but should be tunable per-region
Security: ledger events contain only tenant_id and lease_id; avoid leaking usage patterns across tenants in aggregated dashboards
